title: The LayerZero send sets minAmountLD to zero, contradicting the layer's own rule that unset minimums must revert
content:
Everywhere else in the Grove Liquidity Layer a zero minimum is treated as an error: `CurveLib/max-slippage-not-set`, `UniswapV3Lib/min-amount-not-set`, `PendleLib/min-amount-out-not-set` (A...8.1.2, A...9.1.2, A...11.1.2). A...13.1.4 then constructs the LayerZero send with `minAmountLD` "initialized to `0`".

OFT transfers can legitimately deliver less than `amountLD` — decimal-precision dust removal and fee-on-send implementations both reduce the credited amount — so `minAmountLD` is exactly the field that would bound that loss. Setting it to zero accepts any delivered amount, including, in principle, none.

The function also has no post-hoc verification: unlike the Aave, Uniswap and Pendle paths, there is no balance-delta check, because the credit lands on a different chain where this contract cannot observe it. So neither of Grove's two slippage mechanisms is active here.

This is only coherent when read together with A...13.1.2's mandate that the rate limit stay at `0` until the integration is tested. The inconsistency is a symptom of unfinished code held behind a kill switch — which makes it a specific thing to check before that switch is flipped, rather than a settled design choice.
description: Curve, Uniswap and Pendle all reject a zero minimum outright, yet the bridge hardcodes no floor on the delivered amount — consistent only while the function stays disabled by a zero rate limit.
